title: Routing priority matrix — latency / cost / reliability tradeoffs
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a concise, operational-first design for smart routing policies that balance latency, cost, and reliability across regions and deployment modes. Target audience: platform engineers, runtime owners, and SREs who will implement or tune the control plane routing layer.

Goals:
- Make routing decisions deterministic and explainable for operational troubleshooting.
- Enforce customer SLAs (latency & availability) while minimizing expected cost.
- Provide soft and hard fallbacks for capacity and regional outages.
- Enable per-customer policy overrides (e.g., region lock, cost caps).

Constraints and assumptions:
- Models have discrete variants: fast-low-cost (quantized), baseline, high-accuracy (larger). Each has a cost_per_token and expected p95 latency per region.
- Regions have capacity signals: available_slots, ephemeral_queue_depth, recent_error_rate.
- Customers may have tiers: free, standard, enterprise. Enterprise may require region affinity and SLA guarantees.
- Control plane can compute a routing score within ~2ms; heavy decisions must be avoided on hot paths.

Policy primitives (building blocks):
- Hard requirements: must_satisfy_latency, region_blocklist, model_version_blocklist, customer_region_pin.
- Weighted objectives: latency_weight (w_lat), cost_weight (w_cost), reliability_weight (w_rel).
- Soft constraints: prefer_same_region, prefer_dedicated_pool, avoid_high_error_region.
- Capacity filters: min_available_slots, max_queue_depth, max_error_rate.

Score function (single-value prioritization):
- priority_score = -w_lat * expected_p95_latency_norm + -w_cost * normalized_cost + -w_rel * reliability_penalty
  where expected_p95_latency_norm and normalized_cost are scaled to [0,1] per-request using historical baseline ranges; reliability_penalty derived from recent_error_rate and SLO slack.
- Higher priority_score -> better candidate. Use this to sort eligible endpoints for routing.

Decision tree (operational steps per request) — expressed as deterministic nodes (not a forest):
1) Pre-checks (hard gates)
   - If customer.region_pin exists -> route only to pinned region(s). If pinned region has no capacity and customer.enforce_pin=true -> return capacity_error (do not fallback).
   - If model_variant in customer.blocked_models -> return model_forbidden.
   - If request.timeout_budget < model.min_expected_latency -> return client_error (advise smaller seq length or cheaper model).

2) Candidate generation
   - Build candidate set = endpoints that satisfy min_available_slots and error_rate <= max_error_rate and region not in region_blocklist.
   - If candidate set empty -> go to fallback path (step 6).

3) Scoring and ordering
   - For each candidate compute priority_score as above. Apply bias multipliers: if candidate.region == request.origin_region then multiply score by (1 + same_region_bonus). If endpoint.is_dedicated_pool and customer.tier==enterprise then apply dedicated_bonus.
   - Sort candidates by descending priority_score.

4) SLA enforcement and final checks
   - Pick top candidate. If expected_p95_latency(candidate) > request.latency_SLO && customer.tier != enterprise -> attempt next candidate up to N tries.
   - If none candidate can meet request.latency_SLO for enterprise customer -> escalate to fallback that targets higher-cost low-latency model variant or route to reserved capacity and mark as routed_via_sla_bypass.

5) Commit routing decision
   - Atomically decrement ephemeral_slots for chosen endpoint (or reserve tokens) and return route. Emit trace span with score breakdown and decision path.

6) Fallback hierarchy (single deterministic path)
   - Option A: If same-region candidate unavailable -> prefer cross-region candidate with latency <= cross_region_max_latency and lowest cost_penalty.
   - Option B: If no cross-region candidate meets thresholds -> attempt model_variant fallback (e.g., baseline -> quantized faster variant) in same or cross-region.
   - Option C: If still no candidate and request.allow_degraded == true -> route to cheapest available endpoint and add degraded=true in response metadata.
   - Option D: If nothing available -> queue request (if queueing_policy allows) and return queued token; otherwise fail fast with clear error code.

Operational heuristics and example weights:
- Typical starting weights: w_lat=0.6, w_cost=0.3, w_rel=0.1 (for latency-sensitive workloads). For cost-sensitive batch workloads: w_lat=0.2, w_cost=0.7, w_rel=0.1.
- same_region_bonus = 0.15; dedicated_bonus = 0.25; cross_region_latency_penalty applied as +0.05 per 10ms over baseline.
- Normalize cost: normalized_cost = (cost_per_token - min_cost_ref) / (max_cost_ref - min_cost_ref). Update min/max refs weekly per-model class.

Examples (numbers):
- Request A: user in us-west, latency_SLO=120ms, model=stable-7b, customer=standard. Candidates: us-west-dedicated(p95=90ms,cost=1.2), us-east(130ms,cost=0.9), eu-west(200ms,cost=0.7). With w_lat=0.6,w_cost=0.3 -> us-west wins.
- Request B: user in eu-west, latency_SLO=80ms, enterprise pinned to eu-west. eu-west capacity low-> since enforce_pin=true, fail capacity check and return capacity_error to caller and create alert to oncall.

Observability and metrics to emit per decision:
- decision.trace_id, chosen_endpoint, priority_score_breakdown, candidate_list_sizes, fallback_trigger_reason, latency_budget_used, routing_time_ms.
- Alerts: repeated SLA_bypass_count > threshold per customer, region_error_rate spike, reserved_pool_starvation.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit test: deterministic score calculations with mocked metrics.
- Integration test: synthetic traffic generator that exercises region failures, cost spikes, and capacity churn.
- Canary rollout: start with non-critical customer cohort (internal dev org) for 2 weeks. Monitor routing drift vs baseline and error rates.

Performance and scaling considerations:
- Keep score computation O(k) where k=candidate_count. Limit k by region-level prefilter (max 6 endpoints). Cache normalized scales (cost/latency) to avoid repeated DB lookups.
- For high QPS endpoints compute incremental reservation via leaky-bucket token reserves to avoid races.

Risks and open questions:
- How to incorporate model quality metrics (e.g., regression probability) into priority for gen tasks that require high fidelity?
- Cost normalization across heterogeneous hardware is noisy; require continuous re-calibration and guardrails to avoid routing thrash when spot prices fluctuate.
- How should we expose policy tuning to customers (safe knobs vs full control)?

Next steps / action items:
- PR to implement priority_score and candidate prefilter in routing-service (ENG-4310) assigned to Priya.
- Add trace fields and dashboard templates (SRE) to visualize fallback reasons.
- Draft customer-facing KB for region pin behavior and enforced-pinned-region failure modes.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an operational-first design intended to be conservative by default (prefer failing fast over silent degradation for enterprise pinned regions).
- Feedback requested on the score normalization approach and the weights recommended per workload class.

End of note.
